comparator.name: Theologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 OER, established on 9 July 2026 and effective from 1 September 2026, defines a three-year, 180-EC Dutch bachelor in Utrecht. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC theological foundation. Year 2 combines one 24-EC disciplinary track, Greek (15 EC), Hebrew (15 EC) and 6 EC of personal development and worldview; the OER also permits a no-language replacement pathway, but that is an alternative rather than the primary formal table used here. Year 3 consists of a 30-EC minor, 9 EC in exegesis and source languages, a 6-EC theology/media/current-affairs component and a 15-EC final project. The generic registry target names no track. All four tracks carry the same formal weight, so Systematische Theologie, the first track in the OER's official list, is selected by a neutral source-order tie-break fixed independently of UCR fit. The current target and official sources specify the Utrecht programme; registry interest evidence still points to an older Groningen partnership page, so those stale Groningen-specific interests do not override the authoritative Utrecht curriculum. The selected primary language pathway remains unchanged. It must not be generalized to every bachelor route: the explicit language-free option replaces Greek/Hebrew 30 EC with four additional track courses (24 EC) and Interreligieuze praktijken (6 EC), and replaces source-language exegesis 9 EC with a previously untaken track course (6 EC) and Recente eigen theologische publicatie (3 EC). Languages and exegesis are required for the predikantsmaster exit profile, rather than universally for all bachelor students. These mutually exclusive replacements are not added to the selected 180-EC route. The current adopted OER was rechecked on 2026-10-08; the UCR assessment retains its original date and evidence.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Utrecht bachelor Theologie and names no disciplinary track. The 2026-2027 OER requires 24 EC in one of four tracks—Systematische Theologie, Historische Theologie, Praktische Theologie or Bijbelwetenschappen—and gives them equal formal weight. No source identifies a default or broader track. The neutral official-order tie-break therefore selects Systematische Theologie, the first listed track, before UCR fit is considered. The main Greek-and-Hebrew pathway in the formal curriculum table is retained; the OER's no-language option is an explicit replacement route rather than the selected primary pathway.

exception.reason: The selected Systematische Theologie pathway with Greek and Hebrew is defined by sustained Protestant Christian theology and theology-specific method: systematic, historical, practical and biblical theology; Greek and Hebrew; exegesis in the source languages; theology, aesthetics and culture; Reformation history; Judaism and Islam in theological context; personal worldview formation; and a 15-EC final theological project. Only the 30-EC minor is broadly open. UCR offers adjacent philosophy, ethics, history, sociology, politics, literature, art history and cultural analysis, but no sustained theology, scripture, source-language, exegesis or pastoral curriculum. A 24-course UCR schedule assembled from neighbouring humanities and social sciences would erase the target's defining theological sequence and would not be a defensible substantive match.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected language pathway in the current 2026–2027 OER accounts for exactly 180 EC: fixed first-year foundation 60; second year selected Systematische Theologie track 24 + Greek 15 + Hebrew 15 + personal development/worldview 6; third year minor 30 + source-language exegesis 9 + theology in public context 6 + final project 15. Biblical languages and source-language exegesis are requirements of this selected pathway and the predikantsmaster exit profile, not every available bachelor route. The language-free alternative replaces languages with four additional track courses 24 + Interreligieuze praktijken 6, and exegesis with a previously untaken track course 6 + Recente eigen theologische publicatie 3. Those replacement units are not stacked onto the selected route. The normalized target and current authoritative sources identify Utrecht; stale Groningen partnership interests do not override that identity.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook course rows, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111, GOSPHIL212, GOSPHIL214, GOSPHIL311 and GOSPHIL313 support philosophy, ethics, mind, emotion, agency and the self; GOSHIST111, GOSHIST211 and GOSHIST312 support historical inquiry; GOSSOCI111, GOSSOCI214 and GOSSOCI311 support social analysis; MCCLITR112 and MCCLITR211 engage literary and mythic traditions; MCCHEAM111 and MCCHEAM212 support art-historical and cultural interpretation. None is a dedicated course in Protestant or systematic theology, biblical Greek or Hebrew, scriptural exegesis, historical or practical theology, pastoral formation, Reformation theology or theological research. These adjacent courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course Theology progression.
